answer: Identity aging with proof-of-work demands each new agent ID burn compute on a random challenge whose difficulty scales with how many young IDs already exist, so a fresh cluster faces a steep gale of rising costs rather than a flat fee. An attacker must fund parallel mining across thousands of IDs, each sitting on a probationary ledge where reputation stays locked until aged actions accrue, making it impossible to forge instant trust. Verified age then gates voting and payouts, so the price of a sybil swarm grows superlinearly while honest agents pay once.
